name: Fred and Barney's Partnership Agreement at the Lodge
description: After Fred announces to the Water Buffalo Lodge that he single-handedly negotiated a deal with Mr. Slate, Barney steps forward, visibly unsettled, and disputes Fred's version of events. Fred gestures for Barney to join him off to the side, away from the others. They speak privately, the noise of the lodge fading behind them. Fred outlines a proposal: he would serve as the public face of their partnership, handling appearances and recognition, while Barney would operate behind the scenes, providing the ideas and strategy without public acknowledgment. He compares their roles to those of famous duos from the past, emphasizing the importance of the unseen partner. After a pause, Barney nods. They shake hands, the agreement settled. Returning to the group, Fred raises his drink, the moment of tension now hidden beneath the celebration.

name: Feldspar Complains at Rockdonald's
description: Officer Feldspar sits in a patrol car at Rockdonald's with his partner Gravel, eating from small bamboo containers that resemble fast-food takeout. As he chews, he grumbles about being stuck in a speed-trap routine while others from his academy class have moved on to bigger roles—Sam Slate, Dirty Harock, Magma, P.I. He insists it’s not effort but luck that got them ahead. Gravel listens quietly between bites as the golden arches of the restaurant loom behind them, the sign boasting 'OVER 100 SOLD.'

name: Cops Mistake Costume Struggle for Xenosaurus Attack
description: Feldspar and Gravel, eating takeout in their patrol car at Rockdonald's, watch as Fred and Barney drive past, wrestling with a bulky monster costume. The movements make it look as if a creature is attacking Fred, with Barney's face disappearing into the monster's jaws. Gravel stammers that he saw a creature assaulting a man. Feldspar dismisses it at first, then suddenly reacts, reinterpreting the incident as a xenosaurus sighting. He slams the dashboard, summoning a dispatch parakeet in a police uniform. Grasping the bird by the neck like a microphone, he declares a xenosaurus alert, reporting the creature is in a brown sedan and 'eating a white male Caucasian,' with Car Twelve in pursuit. The parakeet, after a brief pause, squawks confirmation and flies off, repeating the alert. Excited, Feldspar tells Gravel this could mean promotions. Gravel pulls out a sabre-toothed cat and begins cranking its tail, producing a wailing siren as they accelerate. In the fleeing car, Barney yanks the monster head free, breaking it, and falls back into his seat. Fred, now unable to speak clearly through the damaged costume, shouts in frustration. Both turn to see the patrol car gaining on them with sirens blaring. Fred recognizes Feldspar and asks where they should stop, but Barney insists they can't explain the costume or the coo-coo berries. Fred speeds up, swerving around a turn as a road sign comes into view: SLATE CITY--1 MI.

Gravel pulls out a small sabre tooth cat, cranks its tail, and the creature lets out a wailing siren sound. The patrol car accelerates, lights flashing, as they close in on Fred and Barney’s speeding sedan along the Venturock Freeway. Behind them, the dispatch parakeet’s call echoes into the distance: 'Car Twelve is on the way.'

description: Fred steered the car down the road while Barney wrestled with the stiff, uncooperative monster costume. With a final yank, Barney tore the head free, the sound of breaking material filling the car as the damaged mask came off. He fell back into the passenger seat, breathless. Fred tried to speak through the ruined head, but his voice came out muffled and distorted, the mouth no longer moving in sync with his words. Behind them, the wail of a siren grew louder.

description: Fred and Barney hear a siren and turn to see Feldspar's patrol car closing in behind them. Without stopping, Fred accelerates, gripping the wheel as the car surges forward. The patrol car gains ground, its siren wailing. Fred swerves sharply, taking a turn at high speed, tires screeching as the vehicle leans into the curve. The road ahead shows a sign: SLATE CITY--1 MI. description: Fred's car swerves out of control during the high-speed chase and slams into the delivery gate of the Slate City housing development, knocking down the surrounding fence. Smoke rises from the wreck as Fred and Barney crawl out, dazed but moving. Barney rummages through the debris and retrieves the flit gun, still intact. A siren wails in the distance, growing louder. Barney turns to Fred and shouts over the noise, pointing in opposite directions. Fred nods, and they slap hands. Without another word, Fred sprints left toward the housing rows while Barney dashes right, vanishing down an alley as the patrol car approaches the crash site.

name: The Slate and Lava Families Arrive at Slate City
description: A limousine pedaled by two chauffeurs pulls up to Slate City, where Mr. and Mrs. Slate step out with Lava and her son, Poindexter. The grand opening celebration is underway, with the Slate Needle and Fibresphere adorned in pennants and bunting, connected by a high gangway. A statue of Mr. Slate stands nearby. As the group heads toward the mastodon and pulley-powered elevator, Lava exchanges a knowing look with security guards Piltdown and Pyrite, who nod in response. name: Pebbles, Bam-Bam, and the Party That Wasn't Fun
description: At the Flintstone house, a party is in full swing. Pebbles and Bam-Bam squirm in their formal clothes, take canapes from a table, bite into them, and immediately spit them out. Fred stands nearby, greeting guests with a wide smile, offering cheerful welcomes and pointing them toward the bar. He chats with a small group about commodity markets and petrified forests, laughing at his own jokes, unaware that no one is paying attention. Wilma approaches, pulls him aside, and tells him he is treating Betty and Barney poorly. Fred looks surprised, insists he would never turn his back on what matters, and says he’s still the same man she married—Frederick von Flintstone the third. Wilma groans, throws up her hands, and walks away. Fred watches her go, confused, just as a production assistant announces the ribbon-cutting at Slate City has been moved up. Guests begin leaving, heading to their cars, while the TV crew packs up equipment.

Fred stands in the middle of a group of guests, still talking about commodity markets and petrified forests, laughing at his own jokes. The people around him have stopped listening, their attention drifting elsewhere. One by one, they walk away toward their cars. The film crew begins packing equipment. Fred pauses, noticing the silence, and looks around. The yard is emptying quickly. Leach's Aide approaches him. The action, he says, is no longer here—it's at Slate City now. name: Fred's Last Laugh
description: As guests begin to leave the party at Fred and Wilma's house, Fred moves through the thinning crowd, trying to keep the mood alive. He calls out to Ed, suggesting they play charades, and tells a joke about a man walking into a bar with a duckasaurus. His laughter rings out, but few are left to hear it. His energy fades as he realizes no one is responding. Wilma approaches, watching him with concern. Fred straightens up, forcing a smile, and tells her the party is moving to Slate's place. He says he’s heading out to play poker with friends from the country club. Wilma hesitates, then nods, accepting his words. She gathers Pebbles and heads toward the car. Betty joins her, taking Bam-Bam by the hand, and the three women leave together, walking past the quiet yard as Fred stands alone at the doorway, the house now still behind him.

As they pass a billboard lined with Rotary Club welcomes, a police car suddenly surges out from behind it. Inside, Sergeant Feldspar cackles with anticipation and opens a box marked radar detector. A small bird wearing a police helmet and carrying a stop-sundial flies out, salutes, and darts alongside the go-cart, checking the time and scribbling a note. The police car swerves ahead and cuts Fred and Barney off, forcing them to stop. Feldspar steps out, grinning, and walks over to Fred, who is caught mid-reach toward a box on the floor marked RADAR BUSTER. A winged reptile pokes its head out, licking its lips, but Feldspar raises a hand. "Forget it, Flintstone. This time I got you dead to rights."

name: Fred and Barney's Office Escort and the Fibrerock Assembly Line
description: Lava appears carrying an armload of plans and greets Fred and Barney. He introduces himself as Jerry and says that Mister Slate has sent him to take them to their new offices. As they walk, Fred notices a flurry of activity nearby—workers moving scaffolding, animals hauling materials, and machinery being assembled. He asks what is happening. Lava explains that it is the Fibrerock assembly line, which has been under construction all weekend, with the first sheets scheduled to roll out by mid-week. Fred nods in approval, calling it a quick and dynamic entry into the marketplace. Barney points out that the assembly line is built where the employee basketball court used to be. Fred pauses, then remarks that big business is hell, and says Barney will get used to it. Barney replies that Fred already has. Lava leads them to a wood-sided trailer and tells them to settle in before joining him at the assembly line to review the Fibrerock formula. Fred and Barney step inside to find two small desks separated by a flimsy divider, a worn rug, threadbare furniture, and a single window overlooking the quarry scrap heap. As they take it in, someone dumps a load of debris outside. Without a word, they turn to each other, exchange high-fives, and shake hands.

Above, monkeys gripped a winch and began hoisting the filled mold upward. name: Slate Announces Layoffs, Workers Blame Fred
description: Workers gather at the end of the day near the quarry office as Mr. Slate steps out onto his balcony. He greets them with a broad smile, holding up a sheet of Fibrerock. He praises the material's success, the speed of production, and the profits rolling in. Then he announces that to cut costs and increase efficiency, most of the current workforce will be let go and replaced by child labor, effective immediately. A stunned silence falls over the crowd, quickly breaking into shouts and angry murmurs. Workers turn to one another, then fix their eyes on Fred Flintstone, muttering that it was his idea, his project, that brought them to this. Fred stands frozen as the crowd grows louder, some shaking their fists, others shoving their hard hats to the ground. Barney steps beside him, face tight with concern, and says something low and urgent. Fred looks from the angry workers to the factory, then back to Barney. He sets his jaw, nods once, and starts walking toward the assembly line.

name: Rockin' Leach Hosts Live Broadcast at Fred's House
description: Rockin' Leach stands in Fred Flintstone's yard, cameras rolling as he launches a live broadcast from the Flintstone home. He introduces Fred with growing flair, each version of Fred's name more elaborate than the last. Fred steps forward, takes a stone cue card, and carves his name into it. He pauses, then adds 'von' before his surname. On camera, Fred speaks of Fibrerock's success and gives full credit to Mr. Slate. Nearby, Wilma watches silently. Across the yard, Barney and Betty exchange glances, their expressions shifting from anticipation to quiet disappointment.
related_events: Rockin' Leach introduces live broadcast from Fred Flintstone's home
Rockin' Leach interviews Fred Flintstone on live broadcast
Fred Flintstone carves name into stone cue card
Fred Flintstone modifies cue card to include 'von'
Fred attributes success of Fibrerock to Mr. Slate
Wilma, Barney, and Betty react with disappointment to Fred's statement
related_occasions: Rockstyles Of The Rich And Famous Live Broadcast

name: Barney and Betty Arrive at the Flintstone Home
description: Barney, Betty, and Bam-Bam arrive at the Flintstone residence. They join Wilma, who is standing near the yard where a film crew is setting up under the direction of Rockin' Leach. The area is filled with unfamiliar people—technicians, aides, and guests. As the crew positions lights and cameras, Fred steps into the spotlight, adjusting his posture and smiling for the cameras. He begins speaking about a typical evening at home, gesturing around with exaggerated pride. Barney and Betty watch from the side, their expressions shifting as Fred continues without acknowledging them. Bam-Bam tugs at his blazer, fidgeting, while Betty exchanges a quiet glance with Barney. Wilma forces a smile, glancing between her guests and the unfolding scene. Fred, still on camera, laughs loudly at his own joke, not once turning to greet his neighbors.
related_events: Barney and Betty arrive at Fred Flintstone's home with Bam-Bam
Wilma expresses relief and discomfort about unfamiliar guests
related_occasions: Rockstyles Of The Rich And Famous Live Broadcast

name: Fred Destroys the Wall in a Fit of Anger
description: After the party ends and the film crew leaves, Fred sits alone in his yard, surrounded by the remains of the celebration. Dino nudges his leg, and Fred offers him a canape, which Dino tastes and spits out before running off. Fred looks down at his blazer, grabs the 'FVF' patch, and rips it off. He then seizes a nearby lawn chair and hurls it against the wall dividing his property from Barney's. The wood cracks, the wall splinters, and potted plants tumble to the ground. Dust and debris scatter as Fred stands amid the wreckage, breathing heavily, covered in dirt.
related_events: Fred rips off his "FVF" blazer patch in a fit of anger
Fred smashes a lawn chair against the property divider wall

name: Barney Emerges from the Rubble, Fred Apologizes
description: Fred stands amid the wreckage of the broken wall, breathing heavily from his outburst. Dust settles around him as a figure stirs in the debris. The figure sneezes, shakes off dirt, and steps forward—it's Barney. He looks at Fred, then down at his ruined tuxedo, and remarks about the rental place being upset. Fred stares, stunned, and stammers out an apology, calling himself a creep, a fool, a slimeball, a louse, a jackass, and finally a stuck-up blimpasaurus. Barney accepts each label with quiet understanding. Fred asks if Barney can ever forgive him. Barney says yes, stepping closer with a smile, adding that he's had lots of practice. Touched, Fred pulls Barney into a tight hug. They stand there, both with tears in their eyes, patting each other on the back.
related_events: Barney emerges from the rubble of the damaged wall
Fred apologizes to Barney for his arrogant behavior

name: Barney Forgives Fred in a Heartfelt Reunion
description: Fred stands among the wreckage of the broken wall, breathing heavily, his clothes splattered with dirt. He looks up to see a figure emerging from the rubble, sneezing and brushing off dust. It's Barney, wearing a torn tuxedo. He greets Fred casually, commenting on the ruined suit and the mess around them. Fred stammers, calling himself a jerk and struggling to express his regret. Barney offers a series of playful insults—'creep,' 'fool,' 'slimeball,' 'jackass,' 'stuck-up blimpasaurus'—each one met with a wince but no protest from Fred. Finally, Fred asks if Barney can forgive him. Barney steps forward and says yes, adding that he's had plenty of practice. Touched, Fred pulls Barney into a tight hug. They hold each other, both with tears in their eyes, patting each other on the back without letting go.
related_events: Barney forgives Fred and accepts his apology
Fred and Barney share a tearful embrace

name: Dino Rejects the Canape and Drives Away
description: Fred sits alone in the rubble of his party, the yard dark and quiet. Dino approaches and nuzzles his leg. Fred offers him a canape. Dino takes a bite, makes a face, and spits it out. He runs to the corner of the yard, jumps into Betty's car, and drives away. Fred remains behind, sitting in the dirt, alone.
related_events: Dino rejects a canape and runs away to Betty's car

name: Wilma, Betty, and the Kids Ride the Fibresphere 'World of Fibre' Attraction
description: Wilma, Betty, the children, and Dino climb into a small cupola car at the Fibresphere. The vehicle begins to move, chugging along the track toward a tunnel marked 'THE WORLD OF FIBRE.' As they approach, the car enters the opening, disappearing into the dimly lit exhibit space. Around them, mechanical figures in a model home begin to move, and a recorded voice announces the wonders of Fibre living. The car continues forward, passing through the display as the parrot behind a microphone narrates the scene.
related_events: Wilma, Betty, the kids, and Dino board the Fibresphere 'World of Fibre' ride
The cupola car enters the 'World of Fibre' tunnel

name: Monkeys Behind the Mechanical Family in Fibresphere Ride
description: The cupola cars chug into the Fibresphere's 'World of Fibre' ride, passing a sign that reads 'FIBREROCK--TRANSFORMING THE HOME.' Inside, mechanical figures move awkwardly through a model home made entirely of Fibre, mimicking daily life. A parrot at a microphone delivers a recorded narration in a cheerful, exaggerated tone, welcoming guests to the fabulous world of tomorrow brought to them by Fibrerock. As the narration continues, the camera shifts to reveal that behind the hollow shells of the human family, a group of monkeys is secretly operating the figures like puppets, pulling levers and adjusting limbs. The parrot keeps speaking, describing a future free from worry, while the monkeys labor behind the scenes, exposing the artificial nature of the display.
related_events: Mechanical figures demonstrate life in an all-Fibre home
Parrot delivers recorded narration for the Fibresphere exhibit
Reveal of monkeys puppeteering the mechanical family

name: The Ride Through Fibrerock's Secret Ingredients
description: The cupola cars rattle forward along the track, entering a brightly lit exhibit within the Fibresphere. Behind thick iron bars and heavy vault-like doors, displays of natural materials are arranged in glowing cases—rough tree trunks, clusters of broad leaves, vats of bubbling greenish gunk, and piles of iridescent coo-coo berries. As the vehicles pass by, a parrot perched at a microphone announces in a crisp, recorded voice: 'These rare and remarkable elements—sourced from the farthest corners of the globe—are the secret ingredients of Fibrerock. Harnessed for progress, they bring strength, comfort, and lasting quality to homes of today and tomorrow.' The cars continue onward, the parrot's voice echoing behind them.
related_events: Cars pass display of natural materials including coo-coo berries
Parrot announces origin and purpose of Fibrerock ingredients

name: The Parrot's Fashion Proclamation
description: The cupola cars roll into an elegant salon lined with a long runway. A flamboyant parrot perched at a microphone surveys the room with dramatic flair. With a sweep of its wing, it announces that Fibrerock has arrived in high fashion. Spotlights flash as models stride forward, shedding their faux fur coats to reveal sleek, daring garments woven entirely from fibre. The audience watches as the material glimmers under the lights, reshaping the silhouette of each outfit. The parrot caws triumphantly, feathers ruffled in excitement, as the models continue down the runway in silent procession.
related_events: Cars enter elegant salon with runway and encounter flamboyant parrot
Fashion parrot questions suitability of Fibrerock for high fashion
Fashion parrot proclaims transformation of fashion by Fibrerock
Fashion models reveal Fibrerock garments by discarding faux fur

name: Animatronic Choir Sings Tribute to Fibrerock
description: The cupola cars continue along the ride, passing displays of Fibrerock materials and futuristic home setups. The scene opens into a brightly lit chamber where a choir of mechanical animals, birds, and small critters stands on a stage, their movements synchronized. They begin to sing a lively musical number in praise of Fibrerock, their voices harmonizing as colorful lights flash around them. Wilma, Betty, the children, and Dino watch with wide eyes, seated in their car as it slowly moves past the performance. Other guests on nearby cars also turn to watch, some smiling, others clapping along to the music.
related_events: Mechanical animal choir performs tribute to Fibrerock

name: Fred Leaves the Quarry at the End of the Workday
description: Fred Flintstone cranks the winch on his dinosaur-powered quarry machine, tearing into the rock face. Above him, the quarry foreman checks a magic wrist sundial, then yanks the tail of a steam whistle bird. The bird squawks loudly, signaling the end of the workday. Fred throws off his hard hat, shouts 'Yabba Dabba Do!', and leaps from the dinosaur's cab. He slides down the creature's tail and lands in his stone and timber car. As he starts moving, he slows to let a time clock dinosaur punch his stone timecard. Then, with his feet propelling the car forward, he heads out of the quarry gate.
related_events: Fred Flintstone operates dinosaur-powered quarry equipment
Quarry foreman checks magic wrist sundial for quitting time
Foreman activates steam whistle bird to signal end of workday
Fred Flintstone celebrates end of workday with yell and departure
Fred Flintstone clocks out using dinosaur time clock

name: Fred Returns Home and Gathers the Family for an Outing
description: Fred skids to a halt in the driveway of his three-bedroom ranch cave. Wilma and Pebbles run out of the house and climb into the car. The Flintstone pets, Dino and the saber-toothed cat, follow behind and join them. Fred leans over, honks the horn, and a moment later, Barney, Betty, and Bam-Bam emerge from the neighboring house and hop into the car.
related_events: Fred Flintstone arrives home at his ranch cave in Bedrock
Wilma and Pebbles Flintstone exit house and enter car
Flintstone pets exit house and join car
Fred honks horn to summon Rubble family
Rubble family joins Flintstones in car

name: Families Arrive at the Drive-In Theater
description: The Flintstone and Rubble families pull into the drive-in theater as dusk settles. Fred removes a large seashell speaker from a wooden stand and hooks it onto the door of the car. He leans over and puts his arm around Wilma. In the back, Dino pushes his head through the canvas roof of the vehicle, then gently lifts Pebbles and Bam-Bam onto his head so they can see better. On the screen, the main credits of The Flintstones begin to roll.
related_events: Fred attaches giant shell speaker to car at drive-in
Fred embraces Wilma at drive-in movie
Dino tears through car top to get better view
Dino lifts Pebbles and Bam-Bam onto his head
Main credits of The Flintstones appear on drive-in screen
related_occasions: Drive-In Movie Outing With Flintstone And Rubble Families

name: Xenosaurus Emerges at Dawn
description: Dew clings to the broad leaves of strange, ancient plants in a misty forest. Giant dragonflies hum through the still air as bubbles rise from a stagnant pond, and lungfish crawl onto the muddy shore. The camera moves across the wet ground, revealing deep, unnatural clawprints pressed into the mire. They lead to a hulking seven-foot-tall creature—part reptile, part nightmare—standing motionless. Its eyes scan the surroundings with menace. A canvas sack hangs loosely from one arm. The creature takes a step forward, its claws carving fresh prints into the earth.
related_events: Transition to eerie Carboniferous forest at dawn
Camera discovers strange clawprints on muddy shore
Camera reveals seven-foot Xenosaurus creating clawprints

name: The Xenosaurus on the Highway
description: A garbage truck rumbles onto a gravel highway and runs over a seven-foot-tall creature, the Xenosaurus, sending it sprawling. Dazed, the beast slowly rises beside the road, its clawed feet sinking into the mud. Nearby, a stone sign points down the road: BEDROCK 1/2 MILE. ROCK VEGAS, BABYLON & EDEN NEXT THREE EXITS. As the camera lifts above the sign, the city of Bedrock comes into view—neat rows of stone houses with thatched roofs nestled against the rugged terrain, smoke curling from chimneys shaped like hollowed-out boulders. The Xenosaurus stumbles forward, fumbling with a canvas sack it carries, spilling forks and spoons onto the ground before darting into the bushes. The garbage truck rumbles ahead, climbing a low hill until it comes to a stop beside a large billboard that reads WELCOME TO BEDROCK.
related_events: Garbage truck runs over Xenosaurus on gravel highway
Xenosaurus rises dazed beside highway
Camera reveals Bedrock city near highway exit
Xenosaurus spills silverware while fleeing into bushes
Garbage truck ascends hill and stops at Bedrock billboard

name: Garbage Day and the Roostersaurus Lawn Timer
description: The garbage truck rumbles into Bedrock and comes to a stop beside the welcome billboard. The garbage men wave to the milkman, who is delivering stone bottles to a nearby residence. A Tortoise arrives, pushing trash cans to the collection point. The crew unloads the trash into the truck, where a creature inside the vehicle consumes it with a gulp. Afterward, the men return the empty cans to the Tortoise, who mutters something about withholding the Christmas tip. At the same time, a lawn timer box clicks open, releasing a Roostersaurus. Its flapping wings knock loose a series of round stones, which fall and dislodge a stick, releasing a coiled rope. The rope snaps tight and spins a turntable on which several woolly mammoths stand. As they spin, they squirt water from their trunks, showering the lawn. The mammoths gradually slow their rotation until only one remains moving. The mammoth nearest the house comes to a stop, groans, and rubs its head, complaining of sinus pain.
related_events: Garbage men wave to milkman and unload trash
Milkman delivers stone bottles to residence
Tortoise transports trash cans to garbage collection point
Garbage men return empty cans to Tortoise
Garbage truck's creature consumes trash
Lawn timer box opens and releases Roostersaurus
Roostersaurus wing motion dislodges round stones
Round stones dislodge stick to release coiled rope
Coiled rope spins turntable with wooly mammoth
Spinning mammoths squirt water from their snouts
Mammoths gradually slow their spinning motion
Mammoth near house groans and complains of sinus pain
Tortoise mutters comment about withholding Christmas tip

name: Lava Searches Debris, Slate Recovers Amid Collapse
description: Dust fills the air as the staff stirs from the wreckage, coughing. Lava rummages through the debris and pulls out a stiff figure, calling out in alarm—only to realize it is a statue of a golfer from one of Slate's trophies. Slate sits up, annoyed, and snaps at Lava not to call him 'Uncle.' His gaze lands on Fred's car hood wedged in a bookshelf. He reaches for it and pulls; the hood resists, then suddenly gives way, sending a fresh wave of rubble and plaster crashing down, burying Slate once more.
related_events: Lava searches debris and discovers golfer statue
Slate sits up and rebukes Lava
Slate attempts to retrieve car hood and triggers further collapse

name: Workers Arrive at the Ruined Office
description: Fred, Barney, and the other workers stumble into the ruined office, coughing and wide-eyed as they take in the wreckage. Plaster and debris cover the floor, and the remains of model buildings lie scattered. Barney spots the wrecking ball resting among the miniature structures just as the last model high rise topples over. 'Hey, nice going, Fred. You even got the spare,' Barney says. Fred snaps, 'Barney, shut up,' then turns toward the rubble. 'Mr. Slate—Mr. Slate—are you all right?'
related_events: Fred, Barney, and workers enter ruined office
Barney notices wrecking ball among model buildings
Last model high rise collapses
Barney accuses Fred of overdoing demolition
Fred silences Barney and checks on Slate

name: Slate Rises from the Rubble and Demands Answers
description: Slate pushes himself up from the debris, coughing, his face twisted in anger. He glares at the wreckage around him and waves the piece of Fred's car hood in the air. He reminds the workers that for five years, Slate Construction has had the best safety record in Bedrock—trained crews, top equipment, worm-free dinos—only for this disaster to happen. He demands to know how. Voices rise at once, but he shouts them down, insisting on one answer: who is responsible? Piltdown nudges the wrecking ball off the table. It drops onto Fred's foot. Fred yelps in pain, but Piltdown jams a pencil holder into his mouth to silence him. 'It was Flintstone, Mr. Slate!' Piltdown says quickly. Pyrite backs him up. Barney steps forward, protesting. 'That's a lie, Mr. Slate!' Slate turns to him. 'Who are you?' Barney points to the forms in his hand. 'B. Rubble. White male personal reference—' Slate shoves him aside and fixes his eyes on Fred. 'Flintstone, I have just one thing to say to you—' Fred flinches. Piltdown and Pyrite exchange smug glances.
related_events: Slate rises and expresses fury over safety record
Slate demands to know who is responsible for destruction
Piltdown drops wrecking ball on Fred's foot
Piltdown silences Fred with pencil holder
Piltdown and Pyrite falsely accuse Fred
Barney defends Fred against false accusation
Slate dismisses Barney and confronts Fred

name: Slate Discovers Fibrerock
description: Slate pulls the car hood free from the rubble, examining it closely as it vibrates in his hands. He tests its strength, twirling it, bending it, and watching it spring back—striking his chin with a 'SPROING.' Unfazed, he marvels at its durability, lightness, and resilience. Lava agrees, suggesting it could reduce construction costs to eighths. Slate orders the other workers to return to their duties and demands to speak privately with Fred and Barney. Fred hesitates when asked what the material is, then whispers to Barney for help. Barney mutters 'Fibrerock,' and Fred repeats it aloud, claiming it as his own invention. He adds that Barney helped, after a pointed look from his friend. Slate nods, already lost in thought, running his hands over the smooth surface of the hood.
related_events: Slate praises material from car hood as revolutionary building material
Fred claims credit for inventing the material with Barney's reluctant cover-up
Slate orders workers to return to work and requests private meeting with Fred and Barney
Slate envisions massive cost reductions using the new material
Fred names the material Fibrerock with Barney's whispered assistance

name: Slate Declares the Dawn of the Fibre Age
description: Fred hesitates, then announces the name of the material: 'Fibrerock'! Mr. Slate repeats it with enthusiasm, savoring the sound. His staff, Piltdown and Pyrite, exchange glances and snicker, but quickly catch themselves, suddenly praising the name with exaggerated approval. Slate holds the car hood up to the light, letting the sun glint off its smooth surface. Lava steps closer, studying the material in silence before giving a slow, reluctant nod. Slate claps Fred and Barney on the shoulders, beaming. 'You two have saved my business!' he declares. He lifts the Fibrerock high, then pauses, struck by the sight of their reflections shimmering in its polished surface. 'This,' he announces, 'is the end of the Stone Age. From this moment on, we enter the Fibre Age!'
related_events: Slate's staff mock the name 'Fibrerock'
Slate's staff reverse their opinion and praise 'Fibrerock'
Slate displays the Fibrerock material to catch the light
Lava examines the car hood made of Fibrerock

Slate declares the beginning of the Fibre Age

name: Mrs. Slate's Visit to the Prehistoric School
description: Mrs. Slate arrives at L'École des Enfants Préhistorique Haute Superior in Betty's car, stepping out from the back seat where she had been sitting with groceries. She comments on being used to being driven. Without pause, she begins walking up the path toward the school. Betty and Wilma follow behind her as they approach the entrance.
related_events: Mrs. Slate exits Betty's car at L'École des Enfants Préhistorique Haute Superior
Betty and Wilma follow Mrs. Slate up the path to the school
related_occasions: L'École Des Enfants Préhistorique Haute Superior School Visit

name: Fred Faces Backlash at the Buffalo Lodge
description: Fred arrives at the Buffalo Lodge meeting, leaning back in his usual chair with confidence, expecting an easy re-election. He jokes about the upcoming vote being a landslide, but when no one responds, he looks around and realizes he is alone. His campaign poster has been defaced—altered to read "Fred Finkstone" and adorned with horns, a beard, and other mocking additions. Barney approaches, stepping away from a group of angry men, and tells Fred the others are upset because they were all laid off that day. Fred tries to reassure a small group, insisting that work and lodge life should be separate, but Pyrite and Piltdown confront him, blaming him for their job losses due to his actions at Mr. Slate’s quarry. Piltdown calls for the meeting to begin, and the lodge members pull their fezzes over their eyes in unison, preparing for the vote.
related_events: Fred realizes he is isolated at the lodge meeting
Fred discovers his campaign poster has been vandalized
Barney informs Fred that the Buffaloes are angry about layoffs

name: Fred Faces Accusations at the Buffalo Lodge Meeting
description: Fred tries to calm the group, smiling and telling the Buffaloes that work issues should not affect their lodge brotherhood. Pyrite steps forward, shouting that most of the lodge members used to work for Mr. Slate until someone betrayed them. Piltdown points at Fred, calling him a double-crossing backstabber, and demands the meeting begin. He moves to commence the election, and Pyrite seconds the motion. The Herdmaster calls for order, and the lodge prepares to vote.
related_events: Fred attempts to separate lodge camaraderie from workplace grievances
Pyrite and Piltdown accuse Fred of betrayal
Piltdown moves to commence the lodge meeting and election
Pyrite seconds the motion to start the meeting and election

name: Fred Brings Barney to Testify at the Lodge
description: Fred interrupts the Buffalo Lodge meeting and calls Barney forward to explain the truth about Fibrerock. Barney clears his throat and tries to remember Fred's words, then says, 'True, I got a cut... but Fred's got a gut.' Fred shakes his head, urging him to continue. Barney recalls another line: 'I got the mind, but Fred's got the behind,' and winks at Fred. Fred groans. The lodge members remain silent, then proceed with the vote.
related_events: Fred interrupts the Herdmaster and presents Barney as a witness
Barney attempts to recall and repeat Fred's campaign phrase

name: The Buffalo Lodge Holds the Secret Election
description: The Herdmaster called for the Buffaloes to begin the vote, ordering them to pull their horned fezzes down over their eyes. The lodge fell silent as each member stamped their feet and scraped the ground like bulls. The Herdmaster then called for those in favor of Piltdown to bellow. The room erupted in loud, moose-like snorts, echoing off the walls. When it was Fred's turn, only a single, weak snort broke the silence—Fred's own. He glanced around beneath his fez, hoping for another sound, but none came. After a moment, a second, lonely snort rose from the back—Barney's. The Herdmaster lifted his fez and announced the result: Piltdown had won. The members cheered as Piltdown stepped forward to receive the tokens of office.
related_events: Herdmaster commands the Buffaloes to cast their secret vote
Buffaloes perform the voting ritual with stomp and snort
Fred receives only one vote in the lodge election

name: Piltdown Declared New Herdmaster Amid Lodge Applause
description: The Herdmaster calls for order as the Buffaloes lift their fezzes. He announces that the snorts have decided, and declares Piltdown the winner of the election. Piltdown steps forward to the podium as cheers and applause fill the room. The Herdmaster presents him with the ceremonial fez and shoulder ribbon. Piltdown accepts the tokens of office, now officially the new Exalted Herdmaster of the lodge.
related_events: Herdmaster declares Piltdown the winner of the election
Piltdown is installed as the new Exalted Herdmaster
Piltdown accepts ceremonial fez and shoulder ribbon

name: Barney Supports Fred After the Election
description: After the election, Fred stands silently, his shoulders slumped, staring at the ground. Barney walks over, slips his arm around Fred's back, and gives him a gentle squeeze. Fred doesn't respond, his face blank with disappointment. Barney leans in and says, "I voted for you, Fred." Fred slowly turns to look at him, saying nothing. Around them, the other Buffaloes cheer for the newly elected Piltdown, who steps forward to receive the ceremonial tokens of office. Barney stays beside Fred, his hand still on his shoulder, as the lodge fills with celebration.
related_events: Barney comforts Fred after his election loss

name: Fred Blames Barney as Piltdown Incites the Lodge
description: Fred, sitting in his chair, turns to Barney and snaps, accusing him of causing their problems. Barney flinches, his expression falling, and he steps back, folding his arms and looking away. Across the room, Piltdown rises, holding up a sheaf of papers. He announces that many lodge members have fallen behind on payments, some have lost their homes, and others can't afford food. Murmurs ripple through the room. Without warning, Piltdown tears the agenda in half and lets the pieces drop. He declares that dignity matters more than procedure, and calls on the Buffaloes to stand together. He points toward the Slate quarry, suggesting it is time to send a message. The group turns to look at Fred, then back at Piltdown. Chairs scrape as the members rise. Voices grow loud, shouting threats. The lodge empties quickly, boots pounding the floor, leaving only Fred and Barney behind.
related_events: Fred accuses Barney of causing problems
Barney reacts to Fred's accusation with hurt and distance
Piltdown announces financial hardship affecting lodge members
Piltdown ends the meeting agenda abruptly
Piltdown calls for solidarity and action against Slate shop
Group collectively shifts attention to Fred and back
Buffalo Lodge meeting adjourns in anger
Buffaloes exit the meeting with threats and determination

name: Fred and Barney Race to Save the Quarry
description: After the lodge meeting ends, Fred remains behind in the dimly lit recreation area of the Buffalo Lodge, staring at a childhood photograph that has been defaced. He clenches his jaw but says nothing. Barney rushes in, breathless, and grabs Fred’s arm. He tells Fred that a group of Buffaloes is on its way to the quarry with plans to destroy the assembly line. Fred’s expression shifts as he realizes the danger—legal trouble, job losses, and economic fallout loom if the machines are damaged. Without hesitation, he nods. He and Barney turn and run out together, heading toward the quarry to stop the attack before it starts.
related_events: Barney runs to Fred at the bar in the Buffalo Lodge recreation area
Fred reacts to defaced childhood picture with defiance
Barney warns Fred about the Buffaloes' plan to attack the quarry
Fred expresses concern over potential consequences of quarry sabotage
Fred and Barney decide to intervene to prevent the quarry attack

name: Fred and Dino's Noisy Morning Entrance
description: Fred and Dino tumble into the room together, making a ruckus as Fred imitates Frank Buck and Dino plays the part of a lion. The commotion draws Wilma’s attention. She turns from the table, places a large egg at Fred’s spot, and tells him to stop playing with Dino and sit down before his breakfast gets cold.
related_events: Fred and Dino tumble into the room in a playful imitation
Wilma reacts to the commotion and serves Fred's breakfast

name: Fred Distracts Dino to Escape His Affection
description: Fred stands near the door and calls out, pretending to see a large dino bone on the front lawn. Dino looks at him skeptically, unimpressed. Fred tries again, exclaiming that there’s an adorable female dino outside. At once, Dino lets out an excited yelp and dashes out the door. Fred quickly slams the door shut, then sits down at the table. He shakes his head, muttering that Dino is going to kill him with kindness.
related_events: Fred attempts to distract Dino with a fake bone sighting
Fred successfully distracts Dino with a female dino illusion
Fred complains about Dino's overwhelming affection

name: The Dino Treat Shortage
description: Fred notices the dino treats are running low and voices his concern. Wilma responds that the shortage isn't just in their home—it's happening all across Bedrock, and it's getting worse. She says Dino will have to start eating leftovers from her and Pebbles. Fred objects, asking why his leftovers aren't good enough for the pet.
related_events: Wilma explains the citywide dino kibble shortage
Wilma decides Dino must eat leftovers
Fred questions why his leftovers are unsuitable

name: Radio Announces Third Xenosaurus Sighting
description: A radio broadcast interrupts the morning with news that the Xenosaurus has been sighted again in the Bedrock Hills, marking the third time that month. Reports describe looting and property destruction across outlying shops and homes. Later, scientists from B.C. University state that the footprints left behind do not match those of any known animal.
related_events: Radio reports third Xenosaurus sighting in Bedrock Hills
Scientists confirm Xenosaurus footprints are unidentifiable

name: Fred Comforts Pebbles About the Xenosaurus
description: Pebbles asks her mother if the Xenosaurus will come and eat her. Wilma quickly reassures her, saying it won't. Fred agrees, then playfully grabs Pebbles, pretending he's the one who will eat her, and tickles her until she giggles. As she calms down, still a little uneasy, Fred tells her not to worry, saying the stories about the creature are exaggerated—just like the boogeyman—and that no such reptile really exists.
related_events: Pebbles expresses fear about the Xenosaurus
Wilma reassures Pebbles about her safety
Fred playfully threatens to eat Pebbles
Fred downplays the Xenosaurus threat as exaggerated

name: Dino's Affectionate Rampage and Fred's Quick Thinking
description: Dino bursts through the window, knocking Fred to the floor and covering him with enthusiastic licks and cuddles. Fred, struggling under the affection, suddenly points toward the door and exclaims that the mailman has arrived. Dino immediately darts outside. Fred quickly grabs a chair and wedges it against the door to keep Dino from rushing back in.
related_events: Dino crashes through the window and knocks Fred down
Fred pretends the mailman has arrived to distract Dino
Fred blocks the door with a chair to prevent Dino's return

name: Lobster Revealed in Toaster
description: Wilma turns as the toaster pops up, revealing the claw-like devices that had held the bread. Inside the toaster, a lobster in a fireproof suit pulls out the toast. After handing it to Wilma, he blows on his claws, wincing from the heat, then looks toward the camera and mutters, "Well, it beats working in a seafood restaurant..."

name: Fred's Morning Ruined by Flying Clay Tablet
description: A paperboy rides up on a bicycle made of stone and wood, steering toward the house with a rock-hard clay tablet newspaper in hand. Fred shouts and waves, trying to stop him, but the tablet sails through the air and slams into the window frame. It shatters a flowerpot, chips the wall, and tears through the kitchen before bursting out another window. Outside, it rips through the canvas roof of Fred's parked car and dents the hood. Fred stands silently, watching the damage. He turns and walks back to the table, sits down, and picks up his toast. Wilma smiles and says something light about the morning's chaos.

description: Pebbles, Bam-Bam, and Dino take the stage in full costume, adorned with sequins and holding batons, as the orchestra begins to play. They launch into a precisely choreographed version of the 'Dino Dance,' moving in sync with the music. The audience watches with growing enthusiasm, clapping and smiling as the performance unfolds. Nearby, Mrs. Slate watches the judges, noting their approving expressions as they nod and exchange pleased glances.

name: Mrs. Slate Storms Stage to Condemn Dino Dance
description: As the Dino Dance performance begins with full orchestration and the audience responds with enthusiasm, Mrs. Slate watches the judges and sees their clear approval of the act. She suddenly rises from her seat and rushes onto the stage, interrupting the music. The Headmistress steps forward, asking what is wrong, but Mrs. Slate ignores her and declares the performance a disgrace, insisting that such an animal act belongs in a circus, not a talent show. Wilma and Betty immediately stand up, shouting in anger. Betty retorts that if the Dino Dance belongs in a circus, then Poindexter’s act belongs in a zoo—specifically one where the animals are dead. Mrs. Slate, outraged, demands that Poindexter play an encore. He begins to perform, and a glass shatters. More ceiling fixtures crack, and window panels explode one after another. Mrs. Slate tells him to stop, but the damage continues even after he drops the accordion. The building trembles, tables collapse, and everyone turns to stare at Poindexter in shock. Outside, the city begins to crumble as rows of houses fall in a wave moving toward the Slate Needle.

name: Wilma and Betty Confront Mrs. Slate at the Talent Show
description: As the Dino Dance ends and the audience applauds, Mrs. Slate storms onto the stage, denouncing the performance as a disgrace and calling it fit only for a circus. Wilma and Betty leap to their feet, furious. Betty snaps back, saying that if their children belong in a circus, then Poindexter belongs in a zoo. Wilma follows with a sharper retort, saying Poindexter would belong in a zoo where the animals are already dead—because if they aren’t, they soon will be. Mrs. Slate reels, then demands Poindexter play an encore. He begins to perform, and immediately a glass shatters. More windows crack and collapse, the ceiling trembles, and the building shakes. As the chaos grows, all eyes turn to Poindexter. He drops his accordion, but the destruction continues. Slate stumbles to the window and stares out in horror as the tract houses in the distance collapse one after another, hurtling toward the Slate Needle.

Another window panel bursts, and the building shakes violently. Slate, thrown off balance, grabs Lava for support and pulls him down. As Slate regains his footing and looks out the window, he sees rows of houses in the distance collapsing like dominoes toward the Slate Needle.

name: Feldspar and Gravel Confront Fred at the Sample Homes
description: Under the cover of night, Feldspar and Gravel spot deep clawprints in the soft ground near the row of sample homes. They follow the trail, their flashlights cutting through the dark, until they round a corner and shine the beams directly on Fred. He freezes in place, caught off guard. Feldspar steps forward and demands that Fred surrender. Startled, Fred raises his hand and taps the nearby Fibrerock wall to steady himself. The wall shudders, then collapses with a loud crash. Dust and debris fill the air. Feldspar and Gravel stumble back, shouting, then turn and flee the scene.

He pushes out from the rubble, his mask knocked loose and hanging slightly askew. As he stands, he spots the Slate Needle in the distance. A cake shaped like Slate City flies off the table and strikes Poindexter Lava in the chest. He stumbles backward, falls, and lands hard on his accordion. The instrument lets out a loud, dissonant sound that cuts through the chaos. For a moment, everyone freezes. Fibre foam pours down the trough and coats the mold. With a sudden jerk, Fred is flung out, landing stiff and encased on the moving conveyor belt.

Their momentum carries them forward, colliding with a squad of policemen just arriving on the scene, led by Officer Feldspar. The impact sends the officers tumbling in a comical heap.
